message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom not to touch my flute. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, the flute is really important to me. It's not just any instrument; it's an Azumi Atlus, which is a professional model. I've taken great care of it, babying it, and I don't let anyone touch it, not even other experienced flute players. That shows how much I value it and how important it is to me. Now, my mom helped me get the flute when I was 17. I couldn't sign the contract on my own, so she signed for it and set up the payment plan. However, I paid for it entirely within 10 months, even though the plan was for 12 months. That's a significant achievement, especially since it was a $2,316 instrument. I paid it off early, which probably helped my mom's credit score too. So, she did help me get it, but I was the one who paid for it. The issue now is that my mom thinks she can touch the flute whenever she wants because she helped me get it. But I don't feel the same way. I told her firmly that she shouldn't touch it, and now she's calling and texting me, demanding to know where it is and saying things like, "I got it for you, I can touch it whenever I want." She thinks I'm being disrespectful by not letting her touch my delicate and expensive instrument. So, is it right or wrong for me to tell her not to touch my flute? Let's break this down. First, ownership. I paid for the flute entirely, even though my mom signed the contract. Does that mean I own it? Yes, I think so. The fact that I paid it off early shows that it's mine now. So, in terms of ownership, I have the right to decide who touches it. Second, the value of the flute. It's not just a regular instrument; it's a professional model worth a lot of money. I've taken great care of it, and I don't want anyone else to touch it because it's delicate and expensive. That makes sense. I don't want it to get damaged or mishandled. Third, the relationship aspect. My mom and I don't have a great relationship, and since I moved in with my boyfriend, things have gotten a bit better but not entirely. There's already some tension there, and this situation is adding to it. She feels entitled to touch the flute because she helped me get it, but I feel that's not fair because I was the one who paid for it. Fourth, the emotional aspect. The flute is "my everything." It's not just an instrument; it's something that's a big part of who I am and my identity. So, when my mom wants to touch it, it's not just about the physical object; it's about respecting my boundaries and my identity. Fifth, the communication aspect. I told her firmly that she shouldn't touch it, and now she's upset and demanding to know where it is. That shows that she's not respecting my boundaries, and it's causing conflict between us. So, putting it all together, is it right or wrong for me to tell her not to touch my flute? Based on ownership, value, and my emotional connection to the flute, I think it's reasonable for me to set boundaries about who touches it. However, the way I communicate this boundary is also important. Being firm is one thing, but being respectful and understanding her feelings is another. Maybe I should explain to her why the flute is so important to me and why I don't want her to touch it. That way, she can understand my perspective, and we can work towards a resolution that respects both of our feelings. In conclusion, while it's reasonable to set boundaries about who touches your personal belongings, especially something as important as your flute, the way you communicate those boundaries can affect the relationship. It's important to be respectful and understanding, even when setting firm boundaries.
